name: Troll
summary: Across Azeroth, the troll empires lie divided, while the Darkspear now live within Thrall's Horde. Trolls are among the world's oldest peoples, born near the Well of Eternity before the Sundering. They heal swiftly and honor primal spirits called loa through voodoo.

sections.title: Children of the Wilds
sections.body: Trolls first arose near the Well of Eternity, long before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor. They lived by hunting and gathering, swift and agile, and their bodies healed grievous wounds with astonishing speed. Given time, they could regrow even severed limbs. Around the sacred mountains of Zandalar, they turned to primal spirits called loa. Shadow hunters and witch doctors guided these rites, which grew into voodoo.

sections.title: War Against the Aqir
sections.body: In ancient times, troll empires fought a long war against the insectoid aqir, whose swarms threatened to overrun the continent. The Amani and Gurubashi led the struggle and drove the aqir to the land's far reaches. Some fled north to what became Azjol-Nerub. Others went south to the deserts where Ahn'Qiraj would rise.

sections.title: A Fractured Legacy
sections.body:
With the aqir broken and contained, the trolls lost their common cause. Their great factions withdrew into separate empires, shaping distinct cultures, physical traits, and tribal orders for forests, jungles, and frozen wastes. Millennia of separation and rivalry followed, along with territorial wars against younger races.

These struggles wore down troll dominion. Most surviving troll kingdoms now meet other races with fierce hostility, clinging to the ruins of their former greatness. The Darkspear, jungle trolls driven into exile, chose another path and joined the Horde with orcs and tauren.

faq.q: Can trolls really regenerate lost limbs?
faq.answer: Yes. Trolls heal physical wounds faster than most other mortal races. Given time, they can regrow lost fingers and even entire limbs.

Loa are primal deities worshipped by trollkind across nearly every tribe. Many take the form of powerful animal spirits, honored with offerings, meditation, and ritual magic. Priests and shadow hunters call on them for blessings, guidance, and strength in battle.

faq.q: Why are most trolls hostile to players?
faq.answer: Many troll tribes, including the Amani forest trolls and Gurubashi jungle trolls, keep insular traditions and deep hostility toward outsiders. Long conflict with encroaching races has made them fiercely protective of their ancestral lands, and they attack trespassers on sight.

faq.q: How did the Darkspear join the Horde?
faq.answer: The Darkspear jungle trolls were driven from their ancestral lands and trapped on an island under attack by murlocs and sea witches. Warchief Thrall and his orc fleet rescued them from annihilation. Their chieftain pledged the tribe's loyalty to the newly formed Horde, out of gratitude and shared need.

Voodoo is an ancient practice of spiritual and dark magic used by troll witch doctors, shadow hunters, and priests. It joins communion with ancestors and loa worship with curses, hexes, and potent herbal brews to harm foes and strengthen allies.
Trolls train as warriors, hunters, rogues, priests, shaman, mages, and warlocks.

angles.text: Your heritage reaches back further than almost any civilization on Azeroth. While your cousins in Zul'Gurub and Zul'Aman hold to bitter, isolationist pride, the Darkspear carry their legacy forward through the strength of the Horde.
The Darkspear trolls bring cunning, agility, and spiritual strength to the warchief's banner as scouts, shadow hunters, and shamans.
Elven history and ancient myths trace bitter rivalries to troll kingdoms. Elves regard troll voodoo and sacrificial rites with deep wariness.
Troll priests are bound to the loa and shadow hunting. They commune with animal spirits and primal dark forces instead of the Holy Light.
